intent: Standing in-place three-strike two-hand attack combo: overhead wind-up -> first downswing -> overhead reload -> second downswing -> recoil/chamber -> third cross-body strike -> recovery back to the loop seam.

phases.description: From the ready stance, both hands gradually lift overhead; the pelvis shifts toward +X and reaches its +X maximum at f29.
First downswing; upper-body and arm angular activity rises strongly, ending in a low/forward extension around f53.
Recoil and second wind-up; the hands retract quickly and lift overhead again. Hips Y reaches its maximum at f57, with a clear overhead anticipation around f71.
Second downswing; this is the strongest upper-body activity cluster in the clip, while the pelvis reaches its vertical low at f83.
Recoil / chamber for strike 3; the arms and torso reset and gather through the upper body to prepare the final hit, with a clear chamber around f112.
Third strike with immediate follow-through; a cross-body burst, with the pelvis reaching its X minimum at f121 and a clear visual extension at f125.
Recovery / loop return; the follow-through continues to the pelvis forward extremum (Y minimum) at f130, after which the motion decreases and the body returns close to the opening pose at f163.

keyPoses.description: The pose and pelvis return close to f0.

weightTransfer: Using Hips translation as a pelvis / weight-shift proxy: f29 X max = +0.258522; f57 Y max = +0.417867; f83 Z min = -0.208795; f121 X min = -0.319367; f130 Y min = -0.713250; by f163 the pelvis returns close to f0. Under the canonical axes (+X = right, forward = -Y), the pelvis shifts to the right during the first wind-up/strike, then reverses strongly to the left and moves forward during strike 3 and follow-through, then recenters to close the loop. This is not a center-of-mass or ground-reaction-force measurement. No support or planted foot is assigned because the source does not provide a contact/load-force channel sufficient for that conclusion.
bodyMechanics: body-mechanics.png measures aggregate local quaternion change per frame — the summed angular delta for each group — and is used to compare timing, not power or force. Peak timing within the three strike windows is: Strike 1 (f36-f53): left arm peak at f44 -> core peak at f51 -> right arm peak at f53. Strike 2 (f78-f94): core peak at f79 -> right arm peak at f87 -> left arm peak at f89. Strike 3 (f117-f126): left arm peak at f117 -> core peak at f121 -> right arm peak at f122. Because the peak order changes between strikes, the evidence does not support one fixed causal/power chain such as hips -> chest -> shoulder -> hand across the full combo. The safer conclusion is that the core and both arms coordinate with different overlapping timings on each hit.

recommended: timing of a standing multi-hit two-hand attack combo
transition from the first two downswings into a cross-body finishing strike
pelvis translation / whole-body weight-shift proxy in multi-hit choreography
staggered core and arm coordination that changes from strike to strike
notRecommendedAsPrimary: exact weapon or club path, grip, or weapon orientation
exact target contact or impact frame
ground-reaction force, load distribution, or a causal power-generation chain

notes: preview.gif does not render a weapon mesh or target, so weapon geometry and contact are not inferred from the clip name.
The source does not provide an explicit foot-contact or load-force channel, so no support side is assigned.
The aggregate quaternion-change chart is kinematic timing evidence only; it does not measure force or power.
There is an overhead-looking recovery arc after f126, but there is no new strike-level activity cluster comparable to the previous three, so this metadata does not annotate a fourth strike.
The clip is looped, and f163 returns very close to f0, but the loop flag is not used to infer any additional attack semantics.
